gaps.sentence: Don't worry about the dog — it ___ at strangers, but it never bites.
gaps.hint: typical behavior takes the present simple
gaps.explanation: Characteristic, repeated behavior takes the present simple: barks.

gaps.sentence: I ___ her at a conference in 2019, but we did not start working together until last year.
gaps.hint: in 2019 pins a finished past time
gaps.explanation: 'In 2019' is a finished past time, so the past simple is required: met.

gaps.sentence: I ___ to contact him all week, but his phone is always engaged.
gaps.hint: all week repeated attempts until now
gaps.explanation: Repeated attempts continuing up to now take the present perfect continuous: have been trying.

gaps.sentence: She ___ her keys yet again — this is becoming a real habit.
gaps.explanation: The present perfect links the recent loss to the present habit.

gaps.sentence: She ___ to the gym three times a week, mostly before work.
gaps.hint: three times a week shows a routine
gaps.explanation: Frequency expressions like 'three times a week' describe habits, which take the present simple: goes.

gaps.sentence: Every time I visit, she ___ something delicious from the garden.
gaps.hint: every time marks a repeated habit
gaps.explanation: 'Every time' marks a repeated action, which takes the present simple: brings.

gaps.sentence: By the time I woke up, my flatmates ___ to work.
gaps.hint: by the time plus past simple
gaps.explanation: 'By the time' plus a past action refers back to an earlier past action, so the past perfect is needed: had gone.

gaps.sentence: By Friday, the climbers ___ on the north face for six days without a break.
gaps.hint: duration measured to a future point
gaps.explanation: 'By Friday + for six days' calls for the future perfect: will have been.
